findings.text: the seam test cited for surface 1 (tests/standard_names/test_catalog_release.py:300) is test_empty_input_is_an_error, a sanitize_build_metadata test; the github_client seam is injected at tests/standard_names/test_catalog_release.py:714-737 (github_client=Refusing()/Recording()), so the map's only test pointer for the REST transport leads a reader to an unrelated test.

the payload-key anchor (:453-:458) holds for exclusion_by_reason (export.py:453), accounted_exclusions (:454) and accounting_residue (:455-:458) but not for the two keys named first: exclusion_ledger is export.py:417 and exclusion_records :418, so a reader sent to :453-:458 to find exclusion_ledger lands 36 lines low.

the claim's WHERE clause is graph_ops.py:10463, not :10456 (that line is token = str(uuid.uuid4())); the adjacent definition (:10444) and charge (:10471) anchors are exact, so this is an isolated slip in the one clause the open attempt-budget followup edits.

entry 5 omits the caller-inputs line the map's own header (reuse-map.md:3-5) claims for every located entry: grep -c "A caller must supply" over the map returns 4, not 5, so the entry a wiring node would consume states the refusal precondition but not what the caller supplies.

the name-axis sibling is described as invoked at loop.py:1783, but 1783 is its import line inside the local-import block and the invocation is loop.py:1799 (entry_result = await _global_maintenance_call(reconcile_reviewable_name_stage, default={})), so the pointer on the one surface with no caller stops short of the call shape a wiring node needs.
